theme: Saul’s early success; his impatience; the kingdom taken
readingInstruction: Read 1 Samuel 11:1-13:23. These chapters show the best and the worst of Saul. He wins a great victory, then he disobeys at Gilgal. Read chapter 13 slowly, and ask what Saul’s real mistake was.
settingTheScene: After Saul is chosen at Mizpah, he returns to farm in Gibeah. Then Nahash the Ammonite besieges Jabesh-gilead, and the Spirit of God comes powerfully on Saul. He leads Israel to victory, and the kingdom is renewed at Gilgal. In chapter 12, Samuel gives his farewell address. Then, in chapter 13, the Philistines gather a large army, and Saul faces a crisis that exposes his heart.
observation: Nahash offers terms: the men of Jabesh may surrender if he can gouge out their right eyes (11:1-2).
“The Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger was greatly kindled” (11:6).
After the victory, Saul says, “Not a man shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel” (11:13).
In his farewell, Samuel says, “Far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you” (12:23).
Samuel also says, “The LORD will not forsake his people, for his great name’s sake” (12:22).
Saul is told to wait seven days at Gilgal for Samuel to come and offer sacrifices (13:8).
When the people begin to scatter, Saul offers the burnt offering himself (13:9-10).
Samuel says, “You have done foolishly. You have not kept the command of the LORD your God… But now your kingdom shall not continue. The LORD has sought out a man after his own heart” (13:13-14).
interpretation:
Saul’s first victory shows what a leader can be when the Spirit of God is upon him. He is angry at injustice, he acts decisively, and he is generous in victory. “Not a man shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation.” He gives God the credit. This is a king who understands that his power is on loan.

Samuel’s farewell speech is a model of pastoral integrity. He asks the people to testify against him if he has ever taken anything from them, and they say he has not. He then rebukes them for asking for a king, but with a promise: “Do not fear; you have done all this evil. Yet do not turn aside from following the LORD.” And he adds the lovely words, “I will not cease to pray for you.” A leader who loves his people prays for them even when they have wronged him.

Chapter 13 is the first sign of Saul’s downfall. The situation is grave: the Philistines have a huge army and Israel has no weapons. Saul waits seven days, as Samuel had told him. Then, as his men begin to leave, he offers the sacrifice himself, a task reserved for priests. It looks like a small thing. He was under pressure, and he meant well. But the narrative shows that it was a failure of trust. Saul was acting from fear of the people and the enemy, not from faith in God.

Samuel’s rebuke is severe. Saul’s kingdom will not continue. God has sought a man “after his own heart.” This phrase does not mean that David will be perfect, but that he will be a man whose heart is oriented toward God. The difference between Saul and David is not one of skill or sin, but of the posture of the heart.

The lesson is simple and searching: obedience is a matter of trust. Saul feared the people and tried to take control, and he lost the kingdom. Real leadership means waiting on God, even when everything seems to be falling apart.
connection: Jesus waited on the Father’s timing, as when he said, “My hour has not yet come” (John 2:4), and he trusted him in the garden: “Not my will, but yours, be done” (Luke 22:42). Paul quotes the phrase about David in Acts 13:22. The Hebrew phrase “a man after his own heart” finds its fulfillment in the one who always did what pleased the Father (John 8:29). Peter says that the one who believes in him will not be put to shame (1 Peter 2:6).
application:
Think of a time you took matters into your own hands instead of waiting on God. What drove you?

Pray for your leaders as Samuel did, even if they have wronged you.

Ask the Lord to give you a heart oriented toward him.
prayerPrompts: Ask God for a heart after his own heart.
Ask him to teach you to wait when everything says to act.
Pray for those who lead you.
